title: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency: feed exclusively ketogenic lysine
vignette: An 8-month-old boy is evaluated for developmental delay, failure to thrive, and episodic seizures. Physical examination shows ophthalmoplegia and hypotonia. Laboratory studies reveal an elevated serum lactate level. Further histochemical studies show severely reduced pyruvate dehydrogenase enzyme activity in both freshly isolated peripheral blood lymphocytes and cultured fibroblasts. Increasing which of the following substances in his diet is most likely to help this patient generate energy without further elevating lactate levels?

clues.text: developmental delay, failure to thrive, and episodic seizures
clues.note: Neurologic dysfunction (delay, seizures) with failure to thrive is the typical infantile presentation of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) deficiency, an inborn error that starves the CNS of acetyl-CoA.
Ophthalmoplegia and hypotonia are additional neurologic signs of the impaired energy metabolism seen in PDH deficiency.
With PDH blocked, pyruvate cannot become acetyl-CoA and is instead reduced to lactate, producing a congenital lactic acidosis. This is the biochemical fingerprint of the disease.

clues.text: severely reduced pyruvate dehydrogenase enzyme activity
clues.note: This directly confirms PDH complex deficiency: pyruvate -> acetyl-CoA is blocked, uncoupling glycolysis from the TCA cycle and shunting pyruvate to lactate.
This is the crux: the useful substrate must generate energy DOWNSTREAM of the PDH block (as acetyl-CoA) so it does not add to the pyruvate/lactate pool. That means an exclusively KETOGENIC fuel.

whatMatters: PDH deficiency blocks pyruvate -> acetyl-CoA, so glucogenic substrates pile up as pyruvate -> lactate. To make energy WITHOUT raising lactate, use exclusively KETOGENIC substrates that enter as acetyl-CoA downstream of PDH. Among the choices, lysine (with leucine) is the only exclusively ketogenic amino acid. Answer E.
strategy: Two ideas. (1) PDH deficiency -> lactic acidosis; therapy is a ketogenic diet (fat + exclusively ketogenic amino acids) to bypass the block. (2) Classify the amino acids: lysine and leucine are the ONLY purely ketogenic ones ('the onLY Ketogenic'). Alanine and serine -> pyruvate; galactose and glycerol feed glycolysis -> pyruvate; asparagine -> oxaloacetate (needs acetyl-CoA to be used).

eliminations.label: Alanine - glucogenic, your pick
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: alanine is a glucogenic amino acid transaminated directly to PYRUVATE. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: in PDH deficiency the added pyruvate is shunted to lactate, WORSENING the lactic acidosis - the opposite of the goal. The trap is that alanine feeds energy metabolism, but it does so at the pyruvate step, above the block. ✅ Correct if: you needed a gluconeogenic substrate in a normal patient.

eliminations.label: Asparagine - glucogenic to oxaloacetate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: asparagine is catabolized to aspartate and then to oxaloacetate, a TCA intermediate. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: oxaloacetate cannot be oxidized for energy by itself - it must condense with acetyl-CoA to enter the cycle, and acetyl-CoA is exactly what's missing. ✅ Correct if: asking a glucogenic amino acid that feeds oxaloacetate.

eliminations.label: Galactose - glycolytic sugar
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: galactose is metabolized (Leloir pathway) into glycolysis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it generates pyruvate -> lactate, raising lactate in PDH deficiency. ✅ Correct if: a classic galactose-metabolism question.

eliminations.label: Glycerol - glycolytic/gluconeogenic
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: glycerol is converted to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, a glycolytic intermediate. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it can be pushed to pyruvate and then lactate, again worsening acidosis. ✅ Correct if: a gluconeogenesis/glycolysis substrate question.

eliminations.label: Serine - glucogenic to pyruvate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: serine is deaminated to PYRUVATE by serine dehydratase (glucogenic). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: like alanine, it adds to the pyruvate/lactate pool above the block. ✅ Correct if: a serine-to-pyruvate/one-carbon question.

reasoning: PDH deficiency blocks pyruvate -> acetyl-CoA, so pyruvate is shunted to lactate (lactic acidosis + neuro defects)
To make energy without more lactate, the fuel must enter as acetyl-CoA, DOWNSTREAM of the block
Lysine (and leucine) are the only exclusively ketogenic amino acids
-> increase dietary lysine; answer E (basis of the ketogenic diet in PDH deficiency)
mechanism: The pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex converts pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, linking glycolysis to the TCA cycle. In PDH deficiency, pyruvate cannot be decarboxylated to acetyl-CoA, so it accumulates and is reduced to lactate (and transaminated to alanine), producing congenital lactic acidosis with neurologic injury (developmental delay, hypotonia, seizures, ophthalmoplegia). Exclusively KETOGENIC fuels - fatty acids and the amino acids lysine and leucine - are metabolized to acetyl-CoA/ketone bodies downstream of PDH, so they generate energy without adding to the pyruvate/lactate pool. Glucogenic substrates worsen the acidosis (alanine and serine become pyruvate; galactose and glycerol feed glycolysis to pyruvate; asparagine forms oxaloacetate, which cannot be oxidized without acetyl-CoA). Management is a high-fat ketogenic diet (with lysine/leucine) and thiamine supplementation.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid Biochem > PDH complex deficiency: X-linked/AR; congenital lactic acidosis + neuro defects; Tx ketogenic diet (high fat, lysine, leucine) + thiamine; amino acid classification (exclusively ketogenic = Lys, Leu).

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: The stem asks for a fuel that makes energy WITHOUT raising lactate. That requires bypassing the pyruvate step - an exclusively ketogenic substrate.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on ketogenic vs glucogenic amino acids, PDH complex, acetyl-CoA, gluconeogenesis, or Leloir pathway? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Alanine (your pick), serine, galactose, and glycerol all end up as pyruvate -> lactate; asparagine makes oxaloacetate that needs acetyl-CoA. Only lysine (and leucine) enter purely as acetyl-CoA.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: PDH deficiency = lactic acidosis + neuro; treat by feeding the block from BELOW (acetyl-CoA) with exclusively ketogenic lysine/leucine and fat.
